signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Bid
signals.text: AUD/CHF reflects the week's dominant G10 divergence, with AUD outperforming by +1.146% while CHF lags by -0.659%, creating a 1.806% spread. This strength is underpinned by a 435bp carry advantage (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%) and recent hot domestic CPI data that keeps the RBA on a more restrictive footing than its G10 peers. SNB holds at 0.00%. AUD/USD holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7086/0.7009/0.6964 confirms broad AUD demand. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage and RBA policy divergence support continued outperformance. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a flight to safety and unwinding the 435bp carry trade.

signals.title: USD/CAD — ESI Alignment + Bank Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3873, positioned below its SMA20/50 cluster (1.3918/1.405) but above the SMA200 at 1.384. While CAD is currently a G10 laggard (avg -0.505%), its Economic Surprise Index (ESI) remains strong at +23.4, diverging from the USD ESI of -9.0. ING Research notes that markets is likely to be underestimating trade uncertainty for Canada, suggesting CAD could underperform despite the recent run of positive data beats. The Fed-BoC carry differential of +150bp structurally favors USD, and the correlation break vs WTI Oil (z = -1.58σ) indicates that crude's volatility is no longer the primary driver of CAD price action. Trade bias: Neutral/Bullish USD/CAD; tariff uncertainty offsets the positive domestic data surprise. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: US 10Y yields retreat below 4.5%, narrowing the carry advantage and favoring a move toward the SMA200.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + COT Extreme
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3596 is characterized by an extreme volatility risk premium, with ATM IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 5.8%, resulting in a +5.2% VRP. This suggests the options market is pricing in significantly more tail risk than recent price action justifies. Speculative positioning is crowded long (pctl 92, lev_net +46,070), leaving the pair vulnerable to an unwind if US data surprises to the upside. The 2s10s bear steepener in the US Treasury curve (+42.4bp) typically supports the USD, yet GBP holds its premium due to SONIA rates (3.73%) matching SOFR (3.65%). Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol premium and crowded long positioning suggest limited upside. Catalyst: Jackson Hole Symposium 27-29 Aug. Risk: Fed's Warsh delivers a hawkish surprise, triggering a broad USD rally and squeezing the GBP speculative long.
